import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.17

by L. A. Kurdachenko

b) Let $G$ be a locally normal residually finite group. Does there exist a normal
subgroup $H$ of $G$ which is embeddable in a direct product of finite groups and is
such that $G/H$ is a divisible abelian group?

Here a group is *locally normal* if every finite subset lies in a finite normal
subgroup (equivalently, it is a periodic FC-group), and *residually finite* if the
intersection of its normal subgroups of finite index is trivial. Following the usage
of the Russian school, "direct product" means the *restricted* direct product, in
which every element has only finitely many non-identity coordinates: with the
unrestricted (Cartesian) product the residual finiteness of $G$ would make $H = G$ a
trivial affirmative answer.

Only part b) of the problem is stated here.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped RestrictedProduct

namespace Kourovka.«9.17»

universe u

/-- A group $G$ is *locally normal* if every finite subset of $G$ is contained in a
finite normal subgroup of $G$. -/
def IsLocallyNormal (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Finset G, ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ Finite N ∧ ∀ g ∈ S, g ∈ N

/-- A group $G$ is *residually finite* if every non-identity element of $G$ lies outside
some normal subgroup of finite index, i.e. the intersection of all normal subgroups of
finite index of $G$ is trivial. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

/-- A group $H$ is *embeddable in a direct product of finite groups* if there is an
injective group homomorphism from $H$ into the restricted direct product
$\prod_{i \in I} F_i$ of some family $(F_i)_{i \in I}$ of finite groups, i.e. the
subgroup of the Cartesian product consisting of the elements with only finitely many
non-identity coordinates. In Mathlib this restricted direct product is
`Πʳ i, [F i, (⊥ : Subgroup (F i))]`. -/
def IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups (H : Type u) [Group H] : Prop :=
  ∃ (ι : Type u) (F : ι → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Group (F i)) (_ : ∀ i, Finite (F i))
    (φ : H →* Πʳ i, [F i, (⊥ : Subgroup (F i))]), Function.Injective φ

/-- Every element of the restricted direct product `Πʳ i, [F i, (⊥ : Subgroup (F i))]` has
only finitely many non-identity coordinates. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem finite_setOf_ne_one_of_restrictedProduct {ι : Type*} {F : ι → Type*}
    [∀ i, Group (F i)] (x : Πʳ i, [F i, (⊥ : Subgroup (F i))]) :
    {i | x i ≠ 1}.Finite := by
  simpa using Filter.eventually_cofinite.mp x.2

/-- A restricted direct product of finite groups is embeddable in a direct product of
finite groups. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups_restrictedProduct {ι : Type u}
    {F : ι → Type u} [∀ i, Group (F i)] [∀ i, Finite (F i)] :
    IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups (Πʳ i, [F i, (⊥ : Subgroup (F i))]) :=
  ⟨ι, F, inferInstance, inferInstance, MonoidHom.id _, fun _ _ h => h⟩

/-- Every finite group is locally normal. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isLocallyNormal_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsLocallyNormal G :=
  fun _ => ⟨⊤, inferInstance, inferInstance, fun _ _ => Subgroup.mem_top _⟩

/-- Every finite group is residually finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isResiduallyFinite_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsResiduallyFinite G :=
  fun _ hg => ⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance, by simpa using hg⟩

/--
Let $G$ be a locally normal residually finite group. Does there exist a normal subgroup
$H$ of $G$ which is embeddable in a (restricted) direct product of finite groups and is
such that $G/H$ is a divisible abelian group?

Here $G/H$ is *divisible* if for every integer $n \geq 1$ the map $x \mapsto x^n$ is
surjective on $G/H$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.17».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsLocallyNormal G → IsResiduallyFinite G →
      ∃ (H : Subgroup G) (_ : H.Normal),
        IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups H ∧
        IsMulCommutative (G ⧸ H) ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, n ≠ 0 → Function.Surjective (fun x : G ⧸ H => x ^ n) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.17»

G is quantified over Type (universe 0), following the existing Kourovka files (1_40, 19_25); the embedding definition is universe-polymorphic in H with index set and factors in the same universe, which loses no generality.

/-- The element `x` can be separated from the identity by a homomorphism to `F`. -/
def IsSeparatedBy (G : Type*) [Group G] (x : G) (F : Type*) [Group F] : Prop :=

    ∃ (F : Type) (groupF : Group F) (_ : Finite F),

means that every element has only finitely many nonidentity coordinates. -/
def EmbedsInRestrictedProduct (G : Type*) [Group G] (ι : Type*) (F : ι → Type*)
    [∀ i, Group (F i)] : Prop :=
  ∃ f : G →* Multiplicative (Π₀ i, Additive (F i)), Function.Injective f

/-- A group embeds in a restricted direct product of finite groups. -/
def EmbeddableInRestrictedProductOfFiniteGroups (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (ι : Type) (F : ι → Type) (groups : ∀ i, Group (F i)) (_ : ∀ i, Finite (F i)),
    @EmbedsInRestrictedProduct G _ ι F groups

/-- The quotient by the normal subgroup `H` is divisible and abelian. -/
def HasDivisibleAbelianQuotient (G : Type*) [Group G] (H : Subgroup G) [H.Normal] : Prop :=
  IsMulCommutative (G ⧸ H) ∧
    ∀ (x : G ⧸ H) (n : ℕ), 0 < n → ∃ y : G ⧸ H, y ^ n = x

/--
Let $G$ be a locally normal residually finite group. Does there exist a normal subgroup $H$ of
$G$ which is embeddable in a restricted direct product of finite groups and such that $G/H$ is a
divisible abelian group?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.17».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsLocallyNormal G → IsResiduallyFinite G →
      ∃ (H : Subgroup G) (normalH : H.Normal),
        EmbeddableInRestrictedProductOfFiniteGroups H ∧
          @HasDivisibleAbelianQuotient G _ H normalH := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.17»

Expressed residual finiteness by separation of each nonidentity element through a homomorphism to a finite group; surjectivity is unnecessary because the image is itself finite.

Interpreted the notebook's “direct product” in the stipulated Russian-school sense as the restricted direct product. This is represented by `Multiplicative (Π₀ i, Additive (F i))`, whose elements have finitely many nonidentity coordinates.

subgroup of the Cartesian product consisting of the tuples with only finitely many

universe u

normal subgroup of `G`. -/
def IsLocallyNormal (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Set G, S.Finite → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ Finite N ∧ S ⊆ N

/-- A group `G` is *residually finite* if for every `g ≠ 1` there is a normal subgroup of
finite index in `G` not containing `g`. -/

  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

  ∃ (ι : Type u) (F : ι → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Group (F i)) (_ : ∀ i, Finite (F i))
    (f : H →* Πʳ i, [F i, (⊥ : Subgroup (F i))]), Function.Injective f

namespace Kourovka.«9.17»

/-- A group is locally normal if every finite subset is contained in a finite normal subgroup. -/
def IsLocallyNormal (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Set G, S.Finite →
    ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ Finite N ∧ S ⊆ N

/-- A group is residually finite if every nonidentity element remains nonidentity under some
homomorphism to a finite group. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : G, x ≠ 1 →
    ∃ (F : Type) (_ : Group F) (_ : Finite F) (f : G →* F), f x ≠ 1

/-- A group embeds in a restricted direct product of finite groups if it has an injective
homomorphism to a finitely supported product of a family of finite groups. The `Additive` wrappers
allow the multiplicative groups to be represented by `DFinsupp`, whose zero coordinate is the
identity element of the corresponding group. -/
def EmbeddableInRestrictedProductOfFiniteGroups (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (ι : Type) (F : ι → Type) (_ : ∀ i, Group (F i)) (_ : ∀ i, Finite (F i))
    (f : Additive G →+ Π₀ i, Additive (F i)), Function.Injective f

/-- A group is divisible abelian if it is abelian and every element has an $n$-th root for every
positive integer $n$. -/
def IsDivisibleAbelian (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  IsMulCommutative G ∧
    ∀ (n : ℕ), n ≠ 0 → Function.Surjective (fun x : G ↦ x ^ n)

/--
Let $G$ be a locally normal residually finite group. Does there exist a normal subgroup $H$ of
$G$ which is embeddable in a restricted direct product of finite groups and such that $G/H$ is a
divisible abelian group?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsLocallyNormal G → IsResiduallyFinite G →
      ∃ (H : Subgroup G) (hH : H.Normal),
        EmbeddableInRestrictedProductOfFiniteGroups H ∧
          letI := hH
          IsDivisibleAbelian (G ⧸ H) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.17»
